name.evidence: PDF p1 red label 'CASE NO. 398 / NORTHERN DISTRICT / LLANO SECO GRANT / CHARLES J. BRENHAM et al CLAIMANT'; PDF p5 (transcript p1) 'for the place named "Llano Seco"'; Board opinion caption PDF p73 (transcript p67) 'For the place called Llano Seco in Butte County Containing four square Leagues of Land'

year.evidence: PDF p9 (transcript p4) petition: 'That on the 2nd day of October A.D. 1845 Pio Pico, Governor of California by virtue of Authority in him vested made a decree granting to the said Kayser the aforesaid tract of land: That on the 4th day of October A.D. 1845 the said Governor of California issued to the said Kayser a formal title for the said tract of "Llano Seco" ... That on the 8th day of October A.D. 1845 the said grant was duly approved by the Departmental Assembly'. The Board's own opinion, PDF p73 (transcript p67), finds the same: 'he subsequently applied to the Governor on the 4th October 1845 received a grant in the usual form which was on the 8th day of the same month approved by the Departmental Assembly.'

governor.evidence: PDF p9 (transcript p4): 'on the 2nd day of October A.D. 1845 Pio Pico, Governor of California ... made a decree granting to the said Kayser the aforesaid tract of land ... on the 4th day of October A.D. 1845 the said Governor of California issued to the said Kayser a formal title'. NOTE: I did not read the Spanish titulo itself (Exhibit A, translation B); this rests on the petition plus the Board's finding at PDF p73.

grantee.evidence: Board opinion, PDF p73 (transcript p67): 'This claim is based on a grant to Sebastian Kayser. The Evidence shows that in 1844 he applied to the Governor for a grant of the land ...'. Petition, PDF p9 (transcript p4): 'On the 1st day of May A.D. 1844 Sebastian Kayser applied to the Governor of California for a certain tract of land called Llano Seco, which was granted to the said Kayser by Manuel Micheltorena Governor of California on the 26th day of June and 22nd of Decr 1844.' Charles J. Brenham is a U.S.-era purchaser: PDF p11 (transcript p6) 'On the 11th day of April A.D. 1850 the said John F. Pope Sold & Conveyed an undivided 1/18 of Said Rancho to the Petitioner Charles J. Brenham' - i.e. Brenham held ONE EIGHTEENTH of the rancho as one of eleven co-claimants.

land_case.evidence: PDF p1 red label 'CASE NO. 398 NORTHERN DISTRICT'; PDF p2 typed slip 'LAND CASE 398 ND 124 pgs.'; leaves stamped '398 ND'; District Court caption PDF p121 (transcript p115) 'D.C. 398: L.C. 289'. Commission docket 289 matches Hoffman commission_no 289; court no. 398 matches.

outcome.evidence: Confirmed, but NOT by the Land Commission. The Board REJECTED: PDF p77 (transcript p72) 'An adverse decree must consequently be entered. Rejected. Filed in office Sept. 25, 1855' over Alpheus Felch, R. A. Thompson, S. B. Farwell - 'it is adjudged by the Commission that the claim of the said petitioners is not valid; and it is therefore decreed that their Application for a Confirmation thereof be denied'. The District Court reversed: PDF p121 (transcript p115) recites 'the final decision of this Court rendered in said cause at the December 1856 term'; and PDF p125 (transcript p119), 3 June 1859, Ogden Hoffman D.J.: 'The Attorney General of the United States having given notice that appeal will not be prosecuted in this case ... it is Ordered adjudged and Decreed that the appeal heretofore granted herein on the part of the U.S. be vacated, and that claimants have leave to proceed under the decree of this Court heretofore rendered in their favor as under Final Decree.'

corrections.grantee: Sebastian Kayser (Keyser), per the Board's opinion PDF p73 / transcript p67 and the petition PDF p9 / transcript p4. Charles J. Brenham was an 1850 purchaser of an undivided 1/18 interest and one of eleven co-petitioners (Chapman, Warbass, Billings, Bolton, Halleck, Hoskins, Brenham, G. G. Pope, et al.).

notes: Hoffman's 1844 is not a register error but the antecedent instrument: Micheltorena's 1844 order for provisional occupation (petition dates it 26 June and 22 Dec 1844; the Board opinion says 'in July of that year Governor Michelterena made an order for the provisional occupation of the premises'). Kayser also received in Sept. 1845 a copy of the 'General title (so called)', whose character the Board had already dealt with in case No. 196. The operative grant is Pico's, 4 Oct. 1845, Departmental Assembly approval 8 Oct. 1845 - so the register's 1845/Pio Pico pair is right and internally consistent. The Board's rejection turned NOT on the validity of the grant but on the claimants' failure to prove the Farwell-to-Bidwell conveyance (no acknowledgment certificate, hence inadmissible): PDF pp74-77, transcript pp68-72. Chain per petition: Kayser -> Edward A. Farwell (10 Nov. 1844) -> Bidwell (half, 4/11 April 1845) -> Chapman & Warbass (1849) -> Simmons Hutchinson & Co., Pope, etc. Dominant error class again: register carries a U.S.-era claimant in the grantee column, and here that claimant owned only 1/18. No patent copy seen in pages read.

name.evidence: PDF p1 red label 'CASE NO. 105 / SOUTHERN DISTRICT / LOMERIAS MUERTAS GRANT / JOSE SANCHEZ CLAIMANT'; grant titulo PDF p21 (transcript p13) 'Las Lomerias muertas al Este del Arroyo de Sn. Benito'

year.evidence: Grant titulo, PDF p22 (transcript p14): 'Dado en Monterey a diez y seis de agosto de mil ochocientos cuarenta y dos' (16 August 1842). Alvarado's concessory decree of the same date at PDF p20 (transcript p11): 'Monterey 16 de Agosto de 1842. Vista la peticion con que da principio este expedte. ... declaro al Cno. Jose Antº Castro dueno del terreno que forma las Lomerias muertas'

governor.evidence: Grant titulo, PDF p21 (transcript p13), opens: 'Juan B. Alvarado Gobernador Constitucional del Departamento de las Californias'

grantee.evidence: Grant titulo, PDF p21 (transcript p13): 'Por cuanto el Ciudadano Jose Antº Castro ha pretendido para su beneficio personal y el de su familia Las Lomerias muertas ... a nombre de la Nacion Mejicana he venido en concederle el terreno mencionado declarandole la propiedad de el por las presentes letras'. The espediente cover, PDF p17 (transcript p9), reads 'Espediente Promovido por el Ciudadano Jose Antonio Castro en solicitud del terreno que se espresa. 1842.' Petition, PDF p9 (transcript p4): 'on the 16th day of August A.D. 1842 John B Alvarado Constitutional Governor of the Department of Californias ... granted to Jose Antonio Castro in property a ranch or tract of Land called Lomerias Muertas ... That on the 8th day of September A.D. 1844 the said Jose Antonio Castro granted the aforesaid conveyed in due form all his title and estate ... to Jose Maria Sanchez the petitioner.'

land_case.evidence: PDF p1 red label 'CASE NO. 105 SOUTHERN DISTRICT'; PDF p2 typed slip 'LAND CASE 105 SD 50 pgs.'; leaves stamped '105 SD'; filename cubanc_lcf_sd105.pdf resolved 200. Commission docket No. 132 (PDF p5, transcript p1) matches Hoffman commission_no 132; court no. 105 matches.

outcome.evidence: PDF p8 (transcript p3), San Francisco March 14, 1854: 'Commissioner Thompson Campbell delivered the opinion of the Board confirming the Claim' (opinion at transcript p28). An order followed 15 Aug. 1854 on motion of the U.S. Law Agent (transcript p31); District Court proceedings not read.

corrections.grantee: Jose Antonio Castro, per Alvarado's titulo of 16 Aug. 1842, PDF p21-22 / transcript pp13-14, and the espediente cover PDF p17 / transcript p9. Jose Maria Sanchez bought the rancho from Castro on 8 Sept. 1844 (petition, PDF p9) and died intestate in December 1852, leaving as heirs Vicente, Refugio, Gregorio, Guadalupe and one other Sanchez child (deposition of Samuel C. Head, PDF p13 / transcript p7).

notes: Hoffman agrees with the case file against the register: grantee is Jose Antonio Castro. Dominant error class again - the register's 'Jose M. Sanchez and, on his death, Vicente Sanchez' is an accurate description of the U.S.-era CLAIMANT chain (the red label itself says 'JOSE SANCHEZ CLAIMANT'), not of the Mexican grantee. Caution for a re-reader: Jose Castro's deposition (PDF p15, transcript p8) says the rancho 'was granted to Jose Antonio Castro about the years 1839 or 1840 as I think' - loose witness recollection, superseded by the titulo he then authenticates in the same deposition, 'a paper ... purporting to be a grant to Jose Antonio Castro dated 16 August 1842 ... marked H.H. No. 1'. The Spanish expediente in the file is a nine-page tracing certified by U.S. Surveyor General John C. Hays, 8 Aug. 1853 (PDF p22, transcript p14), from the former Mexican archives. Grant size: one and a half sitios de ganado mayor. No patent copy seen in pages read.
